title: Member Equities & Patronage Estate Retirement and Loan Offset Terms by Class
content:
Two events can retire Member Equities & Patronage ahead of the ordinary schedule: the death of an individual member, when the estate may ask for early retirement, and a loan of the member in default, when the association may apply the member's equity against it. The terms of each class are these.

## Terms by class

| | Class C Participation Certificate | Class A Nonvoting Common Stock | Class B Voting Stock | Qualified Allocated Surplus | Nonqualified Allocated Surplus | Class H Preferred Stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A deceased individual member's estate may have the class retired ahead of schedule | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Discount from stated value on an estate's early retirement (%) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 0 |
| The association may apply the class against a loan of the member that is in default | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Calendar days a loan must be past due before equity may be applied against it (0 = not applicable) | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 | 0 |

## Points of the schedule

- Only Nonqualified Allocated Surplus carries an estate discount: 6 percent off its stated value on an early retirement for an estate.
- Class H Preferred Stock is the one class the association may not apply against a loan in default.

**Hypothetical illustration.** On an estate's early retirement of USD 5,000.00 of Nonqualified Allocated Surplus, 6 percent of the stated value, USD 300.00, is the discount. A loan past due 179 calendar days has not reached the 180 days; one past due 180 calendar days has.
